questions.learningObjective: Apply intersectionality to a study of intersectionality.

stimulus.body: A 2005 analysis of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% faced combined disadvantages across two identities, while 30% faced only one.

questions.stem: Explain the 2005 Africa finding about intersectionality.

answer.exemplar: A 2005 analysis of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% faced combined disadvantages across two identities, while 30% faced only one. This illustrates intersectionality: the overlapping of social categories that creates distinct experiences of inequality. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates intersectionality: the overlapping of social categories that creates distinct experiences of inequality. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.
